answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns (three ordinary rounds in each of four seasons). Courtship is an event with no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; courtship has ‘no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters; resolve the round-track event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity tile; invite exactly the required number/types of gentry; provide required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy one tile; clean up by sending used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and returning the activity tile to its proper tableau column, flipping/upgrading if required. Only the last player in turn order advances the marker after cleanup. Events precede ongoing effects.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity and Player Reference.

answers.answer: Pass order: servants directly to Available; all gentry in personal discard to hand; resolve round-track event, then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Hiring through Butler’s Room is not a passing benefit; in this base scope it requires hosting its activity. Servants used for ongoing effects on a pass go to Expended at turn end.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Passing.

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, so reputation 6.1 qualifies the PR6 tile and guests for the entire activity even if four Service Help actions later lower actual reputation to 3.4. Each Service Help costs three reputation increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one straight from Expended Service. National Holiday is the stated PR waiver, not applicable here.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions: ‘Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2’ and Service Help row.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; choose order within each group. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative-reputation favour first to avoid a loss: negative favours are mandatory and losses stop at 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable; use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money. If still short and unable to borrow, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments to gain £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments to move one servant from Quarters to Available, repeatable; it cannot take a servant directly from Expended. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments for a full Market refresh, once per turn. Special actions require sufficient reputation; at minimum 1.1 you cannot take one. They are available on your own turn, hosting or passing.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions table.

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room activity using an available butler or underbutler, with no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, directly into Expended Service, with no hiring fee. The used butler is expended and the tile upgrades on first use. Once upgraded, the Room can instead recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service, rather than taking up to two from supply. Unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring, Butler’s Room paragraph.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, or footman) even when that regular type remains available.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring, opening paragraph.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take it from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Quarters at the next rotation and Available at the second subsequent rotation. Passing or a Refresh Service VP card may make it available earlier; once it is in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring, Butler’s Pantry paragraph.

answers.answer: Market price is the Market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve price is £300 plus that modifier. Minimum price is £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate tile you already own; reputation does not restrict purchasing a tile above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve, opening paragraph.

answers.answer: If a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching Market tile and draw again; duplicate copies share one space and its price. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. A Reserve-eligible tile goes straight to Reserve and you draw again. Buying just one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill occurs.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws go directly there except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and later PR1 draws go there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard in this scope, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve and Refresh; Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At every courtship, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall first. For courtships 1–3, score tile VP in the current face-up theme category, including negatives; only a hybrid’s currently face-up category counts. Highest theme score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. If tied, each tied player draws one VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and place them face down on the deck bottom. After courtships 1–3, open the Reserve, fully refresh the Market, reveal the next theme to the right of the earlier themes, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, then advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: At final courtship return the Fairchilds and score tile VP across all four revealed themes; a category appearing twice counts twice, including negative VP. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Ties are broken first by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective. Players then have a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible; move the marker to Wedding Bells and score.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final courtship (round 16).

answers.answer: End-game VP: improvement tiles’ face-up printed VP (including negatives); gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild, excluding dismissed guests); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation by level 1–7 = 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; 1 VP per £200, rounded down; and printed VP on retained unused VP cards. Tie sequence: final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position does not break ties.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Final VP.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup plus two on round 6. Discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card add to the retained final total and do not cause an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together, then placed face down at the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tile(s) at game end, not showing an upgraded side.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards; Base objective reference.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (several cards allowed), and once after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to use its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards remain hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards, introductory paragraph.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use at cleanup; an already upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. Ongoing-only tiles cannot host activities or be upgraded. Hybrids start with their underlined category showing and flip after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) hosts its front activity once, upgrades into the monument, and cannot host again; monument benefit begins on later turns. For a hybrid, only the currently face-up category counts for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects; Scoring → Courtship and seasonal upkeep.

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve during ongoing effects on hosting step 2 after the round event, and on a pass after the event. Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn, hosting or passing; no courtship income, and a newly purchased monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall uses any one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot also serve the activity and goes to Expended at turn end. It cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Improvements and ongoing effects → Monuments and Servants’ Hall.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: footman on tile, one casual guest from hand with that guest’s normal service; doubles all guest favours, including negative ones; upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand with normal service; double one chosen favour and resolve other favours normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest from deck to attend, with no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours and exclude negative favours from doubling; keep guest and place it in discard at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. All three have fixed one-guest counts that cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Suite activity table and following paragraph.

answers.answer: Give the first-player marker to a random player. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, players choose an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Set reputation to level 1, position 1; stack counters 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Each player receives one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; five starter tiles (Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour, Bowling Green) with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Of the four families, Ponsonby starts with £300; other families start with no money. Asquith’s Dowager is an additional family card.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3 and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire receives three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants are returned to the box and are unavailable this game, so cannot be hired later.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; unused servants unavailable.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from the casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player’s hand. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests remain casual guests with a starter icon, not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one, so five. No, you cannot select both Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze; select at most one of them. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments go in the bag but do not count against the setup selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: ‘one double-sided monument per player plus one’ and ‘choosing at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze’; upgrade tiles go in the bag and do not count against this selection.

answers.answer: Draw until there are six different eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack eligible duplicates in the same Market space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort the six spaces by ascending sorting number, starting at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme for open courtship and keep revealed themes in order through the game. Place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is revealed, not hidden, and revealed themes remain in order rather than leaving play when a new one appears.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, the servant in Servants’ Quarters moves to Available Service first; the one in Expended Service moves to Servants’ Quarters. Each advances exactly one space and the Expended servant is not moved twice. An available servant left unused remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity step 1.

answers.answer: The Fair event resolves before ongoing effects and before choosing an activity. If the Private Study is not upgraded at that event step, you receive no Fair reward, and hosting it later that turn does not earn the missed reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Actions → Improvements: Private Study.

answers.answer: Resolve the Draw Objectives event before ongoing effects, during hosting step 2 after service rotation or during passing after servants and discarded gentry return. Draw two objectives and keep both secret with your other objectives. Passing players also receive the event because events resolve on each player’s turn, including pass turns.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table and Round-track events procedure.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday ignores PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so a low-reputation player may use higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain binding, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table: National Holiday.

answers.answer: On Builders’ Holiday, buy any number from Market and/or Reserve within your funds. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling; use one unchanged Market at prices applying before the sequence, including each tile’s space/Reserve price plus printed modifier. Do not refresh between purchases, by special action or VP card. Refill all resulting empty Market spaces together afterward. Market Purchase VP-card benefit follows these same rules.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table; Builders’ Market and Reserve → Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while drawing replacements; refill all six Market spaces under normal rules. Only after filling, return the set-aside tiles to the bag and mix, so they cannot reappear in that refresh. Leave Reserve unchanged.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refresh.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Move clockwise to gain and anticlockwise to lose; passing position 5 to 1 raises a level, and passing 1 to 5 lowers one. Standard minimum is 1.1 and maximum 7.5 (Max.5); ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you can take special actions before or during a reputation favour to make room.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions.

answers.answer: Money is public. Players may not give or receive money between them in this mode. You cannot spend more than you have; a money penalty must also be fully payable. The supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation, wealth and special actions: money paragraph.

answers.answer: For two ladies, family women can fill the requirement because Ladies includes every female family member or female guest. For two casual guests, family cannot fill it; casual/prestige requirements require those guest types and exclude family. You cannot play extra gentry beyond the printed requirement. Family needs no personal service and has no PR, so no reputation threshold applies to family cards.
answers.evidence: Hosting an activity → Invite gentry; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: An ordinary nonscreening guest-invite favour draws one card from the indicated deck, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to hand. A screening invite draws the stated number, chooses the stated keep number, reveals only kept cards, and adds them to hand; rejected cards go to the bottom of their deck unrevealed.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family → Invite Guest favour and screening guests.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so with no unwanted guest you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one just drawn by an earlier favour or a guest from the current activity. Family cannot be dismissed. A dismissed guest goes to the bottom of its matching deck, is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family; Hosting step 6.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer a choice; Lord gives one benefit and Dowager gives both listed benefits.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family table.

answers.answer: The Young Lady draws one casual guest in all cases. She additionally gains two reputation only if a male prestige guest attends the same activity. A male casual guest, female prestige guest, or Charles Fairchild does not qualify; Charles is a male prestige guest, so he does qualify. The casual draw is still received with the admirer bonus.
answers.evidence: Gentry table: Young Lady; Fairchild paragraph identifies Charles as male and a prestige guest.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family cards, so neither has family dismissal immunity; both may be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: Fairchild paragraph.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation yourself. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: base gossips paragraph; reputation rules.

answers.answer: A Barn gives one reputation every time you host an Estate activity. It gives nothing merely for owning an Estate tile or when passing.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Barn.

answers.answer: The Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation directly, in addition to Available Service, without paying reputation; that servant goes to Expended at turn end. Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available and all Expended servants to Quarters, one space each, at hosting-turn start. Service Help instead costs three reputation increments per servant and moves one servant only from Quarters to Available; it cannot take from Expended. Servants’ Quarters can supply one per turn.
answers.evidence: Actions → Servants and hiring: service mechanism table and Servants’ Quarters paragraph.

answers.answer: The Private Study’s front activity requires a butler and two family, with no tile favour. After it upgrades it becomes ongoing, so it cannot be hosted repeatedly; it gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds (spaces 3 and 9) without hosting or staffing.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Private Study.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library: butler, two family, draw one extra objective. Upgraded Main Library: butler, three family, draw one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring; it does not trigger an extra discard.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → Main Library; Objectives and VP cards.

answers.answer: The Objective VP-card benefit draws two objectives, keeps one, and puts the other on the bottom of the objective deck. It adds one retained objective to your final objective count.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, including those in Expended, and they can be used immediately. Service Help costs three reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available; it cannot move directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Refresh Service; special actions table.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, not an underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot provide service immediately from there under ordinary rules.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Hire Servant specifies source, excludes underbutler, and destination. It does not explicitly state immediate service eligibility, though Expended is distinct from Available and ordinary rotation moves it first to Quarters.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest can return one gentry card, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, you may choose it to attend this turn’s activity subject to normal requirements; the benefit itself does not automatically play it.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards table → Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service scoring is 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP → Servants.

answers.answer: Both upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments for the monument objective, worth 3 VP per monument. For a category objective, a hybrid counts only in its currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: monuments and category bonus; Improvements and ongoing effects: hybrids.

answers.answer: Nature Group (11 VP) requires Flower Room plus one garden: English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group (12 VP) requires Gabled Conservatory plus Main Library or North Library. Tiles need only be owned at game end; using or upgrading them is unnecessary.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Nature Group, Domestic Group, and ownership rule.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective scores one VP per prestige guest. The every-three-guests objective scores one VP for each complete group of three nonfamily guests; an incomplete group scores nothing. Prestige guests include a final Fairchild, and guests in hand and discard count for scoring; family is excluded from guest objectives.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: guest bonuses; Final VP; Fairchild paragraph.

answers.answer: The reputation objective earns 7 VP for maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective earns 10 VP for at least £1200. Reputation wheel position does not change ordinary reputation VP, which depends on level, or break reputation tie resolution, which also uses level only.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Reputation and Wealth; Final VP and tie rules.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family. Unupgraded: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their decks. It remains an activity tile on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects → West Terrace.

answers.answer: There is no hand or personal discard-pile limit. Gentry in your discard pile still belong to you and score normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family, opening paragraph.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including a tile under another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only rule. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Open Reserve.

answers.answer: You are not required to host whenever able; you may host an activity or pass. If your preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Hosting steps 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes. A passing player may take the free Market refresh, use the paid Refresh Market special action once that turn, and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each causing a separate full refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action Market refresh; pass and VP-card refreshes do not consume it. However, after beginning a Builders’ Holiday or Market Purchase VP-card buying sequence, you cannot refresh between purchases with a special action or VP card; finish purchases from the unchanged Market, then refill empty spaces together.
answers.evidence: Actions → Reputation: refresh limits; Builders’ Market and Reserve → Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card.
